items.title: Starbucks Sheds More Than 100 Jobs as It Wraps Up Restructuring
items.summary: Starbucks eliminated 104 roles as part of a restructuring effort aimed at boosting growth. The job cuts include positions in the store design and construction team and affect employees who declined to relocate to the company's new Nashville office. This move is part of a broader restructuring announced in May, impacting roles in the U.S. and internationally.

items.title: US Canada Trade Talks Put These Cross Border Stocks In Focus
items.summary: Ongoing US-Canada trade talks have created a mix of relief and risk for cross-border trade stocks after a pause in tariffs. This article highlights three companies – Turning Point Brands (TPB), Uranium Energy (UEC), and Greenfire Resources (GFR) – whose performance could be significantly impacted by the evolving trade landscape, due to their direct exposure to cross-border consumer demand, energy supply chains, and oil sands operations, respectively. Investors are encouraged to monitor these stocks closely as trade negotiations progress.

items.title: Walmart Sales Are Growing, but Stores Aren’t the Engine
items.summary: Walmart reported its smallest sales gain in over six years, with U.S. comparable sales increasing by 2.6%. This growth was primarily driven by e-commerce, membership, and advertising sales, rather than its physical stores. The company's stock fell over 6% in premarket trading following the announcement.

items.title: Valero Energy stock hits all-time high at 351.2 USD
items.summary: Valero Energy Corporation's stock has reached an all-time high of $351.20, driven by robust performance in the energy sector, a 149.73% 1-year change, and strong Q2 earnings. Despite being overvalued according to InvestingPro, the company boasts a "GREAT" financial health rating and positive market conditions, including rising oil prices. Analysts have raised price targets following these strong results, reflecting continued investor confidence.

items.title: Earnings call transcript: AIR Global posts H1 2026 growth despite supply shocks
items.summary: AIR Global PLC reported resilient financial results for H1 2026, with revenue up 3.7% and adjusted EBITDA remaining stable despite supply chain disruptions caused by the closure of the Straits of Hormuz and one-time listing costs. The company's shares rose 2.97%, indicating investor confidence in its underlying performance and management's strategy to navigate challenges. AIR Global also outlined its full-year 2026 guidance, expecting stable shipment volumes and mid-single-digit revenue and adjusted EBITDA growth, while investing in next-generation products like Crown Switch and nicotine pouches.

items.title: Deere Raises 2026 Profit View as AI Construction Boom Lifts Quarterly Income
items.summary: Deere, the largest farm equipment manufacturer, raised its full-year net income forecast for 2026 and reported its first quarterly profit increase in three years. This growth is primarily attributed to an AI-driven construction boom and tariff refunds, which have boosted its construction and forestry segment, offsetting a slowdown in demand for agricultural equipment. The company now expects 2026 net income between $4.75 billion and $5 billion.

items.title: Do Record Q2 2026 Results And Higher Dividend Change The Bull Case For Southern Copper (SCCO)?
items.summary: Southern Copper (SCCO) recently reported record Q2 2026 results with net sales of US$4.29 billion, net income of US$1.67 billion, and a raised quarterly dividend of US$1.10 per share. While these strong results and increased payouts reinforce the near-term earnings story, the article emphasizes that key risks like potential tariffs, rising operating costs, and social/permitting challenges for projects like Tia Maria and Los Chancas remain. The company's narrative projects significant revenue and earnings growth by 2029, suggesting a fair value of $167.79, which is 14% below its current price.

items.title: The loss of low-income diners cost McDonald’s a lot of money last quarter
items.summary: McDonald's experienced a significant financial setback last quarter, losing $310 million in sales from low-income diners. This decline, the first in a year for this demographic, was attributed to a failed value promotion that customers perceived as a price increase. Rival Wendy's faced similar challenges, indicating a broader trend of low-income consumers cutting back on dining due to inflation.

items.title: Leon Cooperman Warns of AI Bust and Recession: 4 ETFs to Take Cover In
items.summary: Billionaire investor Leon Cooperman predicts a potential recession next year, which could end the market's AI-driven growth. In response, investors may consider defensive ETFs offering exposure to less economically sensitive sectors, lower volatility, or traditional safe havens like gold. Four specific ETFs mentioned for this strategy are Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC), Vanguard Utilities ETF (VPU), Invesco S&P 500 Low Volatility ETF (SPLV), and SPDR Gold Shares (GLD).

items.title: Aptiv stock slips after a $300 million guidance cut
items.summary: Aptiv plc's stock (JE00B783TY65) is facing pressure after the company reduced its midpoint revenue outlook for 2026 by $300 million, now expecting $12.6 billion to $12.8 billion in sales and adjusted EPS of $5.60 to $5.80. The revised forecast is attributed to weaker production schedules, delayed launches, and softer software and services sales. Despite the guidance cut, the company achieved $5 billion in second-quarter awards, reaching $10 billion year-to-date and halfway to its $20 billion full-year target.
